thread:
maria: Heads up — after yesterday's test of the offline delta apply we hit ~40% storage bloat on the seed cache. We need a clear pruning/GC policy for air-gapped blobs and a safe apply ordering for partial installs.
jake: Can you paste the sequence that caused the bloat? was it a failed resume or concurrent seed handoff?
sophia: It looked like a partial apply where the index landed but some chunk uploads timed out, agent retried and created duplicate chunk blobs with different temp IDs.
maria: Exactly. Sequence: 1) seed-transfer finishes index, 2) agent starts chunk apply, 3) network hiccup causes timeout, 4) agent retries with new chunk IDs, 5) controller marks activation success based on index only. So orphaned chunks remain.
ryan: If controller treats index as canonical, then orphaned chunks should be collectible once nobody references them. But we need a deterministic retention window so agents don't GC a chunk that's still in-flight for a slow apply.
jake: Proposal: implement epoched references in manifests. Each manifest publish increments epoch. Chunks carry (manifest-id, epoch). GC can safely prune chunks older than current_epoch - 1, unless there's a pending activation ticket.
sophia: Epochs help but what about cross-manifest dedupe? we saw duplicates because retry generated new temp ids not content-addressed. We should prefer content-addressed chunk ids (hash) for storage and map temp ids to hashes at finalization.
maria: Agreed — switch uploader to calculate hash client-side and use that as blob id. Temp ids map to hash; controller dedupes on hash. That avoids duplicates across retries.
ryan: For apply ordering: recommend index-first apply with a two-phase activation. Phase A: index + reservation of hashes (reserve namespace). Phase B: atomic swap to active manifest once all required hashes are present. If reservation times out, controller rolls back reservation and agents can prune their temp chunks older than reservation TTL.
sophia: That TTL needs to consider slow bandwidth sites. I'd rather base TTL on activation heartbeat: agent pings controller every X minutes while applying; controller extends reservation. If heartbeat stops for >Y we mark reservation stale.
jake: Heartbeat model is fine. On GC side, a background compaction job should coalesce repeated deltas into a new base image periodically (weekly) to reduce lookup overhead and garbage.
maria: Sounds good. We also need cryptographic continuity: when we compact, we must re-sign the new base and ensure clients can verify chain. Compaction should emit an immutable manifest that references the old manifests as superseded.
ryan: Implementation notes: 1) uploader uses content-hash IDs. 2) controller maintains reservation table with heartbeat TTL. 3) GC runnable that checks: unreferenced hashes older than prune_window && not reserved => delete. 4) compactor produces signed base manifest and a replacement manifest that triggers a safe swap.
sophia: Edge case: what if compaction removes chunks that an in-progress apply still expects? Reservation table covers that if compactor respects active reservations. Also compactor should prefer low-traffic maintenance windows.
jake: For verification and rollback: agents should keep a small local cache of last N manifests to allow fast rollback to previous manifest without fetching from seed if offline.
maria: Action items: - spike uploader change to content-hash temp mapping (owner: jake, due EOW) - design reservation/heartbeat API (owner: sophia, due next Tue) - GC + compaction RFC draft (owner: ryan, due next Fri) - add integration test: interrupted apply => no duplicates, GC reclaims after TTL (owner: maria, due next sprint)
deploy-bot: deploy-checklist: ensure migration path for existing blobs (map old temp ids to hashes) and add feature-flag for rollout.
ryan: I'll draft the RFC sections and add sequence diagrams. We should also include metrics: orphaned_blob_count, reservation_heartbeat_misses, compaction_saves_bytes.
maria: Cool — let's keep thread here for questions. If we agree I'll move RFC to docs/rfcs once Sophia and Jake sign off. :thumbsup:
